title: Online Sports Betting Is Draining Household Savings
summary: Research summary: state-by-state legalization of online sports betting cut household investing and raised debt and overdrafts, hardest on constrained households.

assertions.quote: For every $1 a household spent on betting, it put $2 fewer into investment accounts.

verdicts.note: Bank transaction data across staggered legalization show this drop in net investing.

Staggered DiD on 230k households across 26 state legalizations: net brokerage deposits fall 14% overall and about 41% for low-savings households, with 2SLS implying $1 of betting cuts investment by $0.99 on average and $3.07 for low-savings households; effects grow over time and hold under alternative estimators (working paper, not peer-reviewed).

assertions.quote: decreased credit availability, increased credit-card debt, and a higher incidence of overdrawing from bank accounts
sports betting tends to have significantly negative expected payouts
which chain together individual events for combined payouts, tend to have much larger loss ratios than straight bets
greater access to sports gambling increased general participation in lottery games, particularly among households that frequently overdraw their bank accounts

verdicts.note: Reported in the same household data; suggests gambling access amplifies risk-taking rather than substituting.

Legalization raises lottery spending, with households that recently overdrew increasing lotto play by about 9% of a standard deviation, while online poker is unaffected; caveat that the data capture only a small subset of lottery purchases.

assertions.quote: many of the “true” odds for a variety of sports bets are unknown, as opposed to the formulaic odds found in other types of gambling

verdicts.note: Sports outcomes have no formulaic probability; the vig hides the expected loss.

The conclusion recommends price transparency for complex bets that consumers find difficult to value accurately, supporting opacity for such bets, but the contrast with lotteries and slots is not examined.

assertions.quote: people can place bets by pushing a few buttons on their phone while lying in bed at two in the morning

verdicts.note: Mobile access drives most volume; the impulsivity link is argued rather than measured here.

The authors argue the online nature of betting plays a critical role in the harms they find and that frictions such as requiring physical presence could deter impulsive betting, but the study covers online betting only and does not compare it with in-person betting.
